ip_top_stories.title: Taylor & Francis and DataSeer extend partnership helping authors to follow journal data requirements
ip_top_stories.summary: Taylor & Francis has extended its partnership with DataSeer to help authors comply with journal data-sharing requirements. The collaboration aims to support researchers in meeting data availability standards during the submission process.

ip_top_stories.title: Thousands of authors seek share of Anthropic copyright settlement
ip_top_stories.summary: Thousands of authors are seeking a portion of a copyright settlement with Anthropic, following claims that the AI company used their works without authorisation to train its AI models. The case is one of several major actions by writers against AI developers over training data practices.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Music Generator Can't Duck DMCA Claim
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has ruled that a DMCA copyright claim against an AI music generator can proceed, declining to dismiss the case. The decision is significant for how existing copyright law applies to AI-generated or AI-assisted content in the music industry.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: A comprehensive review of European Union copyright law developments in the first three months of 2026, covering key legislative updates, court decisions, and regulatory activity relevant to AI and intellectual property. The roundup provides an overview of how EU copyright frameworks are evolving in response to AI-related challenges.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Startups Have These Copyright Lawyers on Speed Dial
ip_top_stories.summary: A report examines how AI startups are increasingly relying on a small group of specialist copyright lawyers as they navigate litigation and licensing disputes over training data. The piece highlights the growing demand for legal expertise at the intersection of AI development and intellectual property.

ip_further_links.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_further_links.summary: An examination of whether the UK government's approach to AI and copyright law is creating obstacles for the domestic technology sector.

ip_further_links.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_further_links.summary: The long-running monkey selfie copyright case is being cited as an accidental precedent in current AI copyright disputes over authorship and non-human creativity.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or regulatory committee has recommended that AI-generated content be clearly labelled to assist the public in identifying synthetic media.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of China's tightened examination standards for AI-related patent applications and the implications for intellectual property protection in the sector.

ip_further_links.title: AI Makes Securing Copyright Protection for Software Code Tricky Guide
ip_further_links.summary: A guide examining the challenges AI poses for obtaining copyright protection for software code, as traditional authorship standards are complicated by AI involvement in code generation.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of a copyright contradiction arising from Anthropic's AI code generation capabilities, raising questions about ownership and liability when AI produces copyrighted-style outputs.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Don't believe the hype. Believe the data.
ip_further_links.summary: An IPKat analysis examines data on AI adoption in the patent industry, urging caution against overstated claims about AI's transformative impact on patent prosecution and examination.

ip_further_links.title: Bologna Children's Book Fair 2026: AI Takes Center Stage
ip_further_links.summary: AI was a dominant topic at the 2026 Bologna Children's Book Fair, with publishers and creators debating its implications for children's publishing and intellectual property. [Metered]

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Exploring Data Spaces in Scholarly Communications
ip_further_links.summary: A Scholarly Kitchen guest post explores the concept of data spaces and their potential role in shaping how research data is shared and governed within scholarly communications.

ip_further_links.title: USPTO Extends AI-Based Search Pilot Program
ip_further_links.summary: The US Patent and Trademark Office has extended its pilot programme using AI-based tools for patent search, signalling continued investment in AI-assisted examination processes.
